task_reconstruction.objective: Simulate a wind-driven 3-D sea surface, translate reflection changes into HF loss/SNR/hop limits, compare ground surfaces, and extend the threshold model to a moving ship.
inputs: wind, frequency, angle, wave spectrum and random phase
power, bandwidth, hop count, ship speed
task_reconstruction.decision: Choose operating frequency/power/angle and path-change timing subject to SNR>=10 dB, while treating broad frequency-table advice separately from computed results.

contributions.summary: Builds a directional 3-D random wave surface from PM spectrum components.
Creates a four-part propagation ledger before component formulas.
Uses Earth curvature and virtual ionosphere height for a one-hop surface bound.
Separates horizontal/vertical Fresnel coefficients before roughness correction.
Uses wave slope and micro-element direction to create a forward-reflection fraction.
Adds occluded-region accounting as a distinct roughness channel.
Maps component losses to a controlled wind/frequency response.
Combines signal field and noise lookup into a 10 dB usability criterion.
Reuses the reflection scaffold with ground material and relief inputs.
Converts threshold distance into a nominal same-path time interface.

edges.handoff: The HF/F2 frame bounds the spectral wave carrier scenarios.
PM density sets harmonic amplitudes.
One-direction components are distributed across directions.
The 3-D surface supplies a local cross section and slope.
Forward-ray fraction feeds the rough-sea correction.
Calm Fresnel reflection is the baseline corrected for roughness.
Rough-sea loss enters the total ledger.
Free-space loss enters the total ledger.
Ionosphere absorption enters the total ledger.
The four-part loss ledger determines first-reflection power.
Total loss enters signal field and SNR.
Dmax and FSPL geometry parameterize the hop controller.
Per-hop absorption is accumulated by hop count.
Per-reflection loss is accumulated between hops.
SNR supplies the 10 dB continuation gate.
Ground coefficients feed the ground comparison results.
Maximum usable distance and hop state feed the moving-receiver extension.
Distance-frequency-SNR states feed Figure 13 and Table 4.
The moving context motivates but does not quantitatively generate the frequency table.
Threshold results are converted into qualitative operating guidance.

assumptions.summary: Retain sky wave as the main route and exclude ground wave from the quantitative model.
Treat F2 as the principal reflecting layer.
Treat wind speed as the main factor controlling wave height.
Fix seawater permittivity and conductivity under ordinary salinity/temperature conditions.
Treat ship movement as uniform motion.
Represent a random sea as harmonic components and finitely sampled directions.
Ignore small E/F offset absorption and use D-layer-dominated loss.
Use La=4 dB in numerical results instead of evaluating Equations 8-9.
Assume equal energy in horizontal and vertical polarizations.
Use one selected 2-D cross section to represent rough-sea reflection geometry.
Use YP approximately 15 dB as a local-time proxy.
Represent terrain relief by the same rough-surface structure used for sea waves.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Wind speed at 19.5 m, gravity, frequency bins, and random phases parameterize the wave spectrum.
Use Re=6371 km, F2 virtual height, and minimum elevation generally above 3 degrees.
Use La=4 dB and ignore <=1 dB E/F offset absorption.
Use YP=15 dB as a fixed local-time-related term.
Retain 27 first-reflection values over 10/20/30 MHz and wind levels 0-8.
Retain 36 coefficients over four latitude bands, three longitude bands, and three time bins.
Retain seawater, freshwater, wet-soil, and dry-soil permittivity/conductivity ranges and selected references.
Retain 27 ground first-reflection values over three frequencies and relief levels 0-8.
Bind f=15 MHz intent, P=100 W claim, n=1-6, distance, and SNR.
Retain five environment/use-case frequency bands as qualitative input guidance.
Appendix fixes M=1000 frequency bins, N=5 directions, wind levels 1-8, and a 501x301 grid.
Appendix maps wind to h=0.0051v^2 and sweeps frequency/angle with an empirical correction.
Appendix uses a single epsilon=8 ground override despite the richer material table.
Appendix nominally fixes P=100, B=0.003, YP=15, La=4, Fa=80, h=300 km, n=1-6.

models.summary: MU-A-2018-86103-001: HF is 3-30 MHz; the paper selects F2 sky wave and recommends about 0.85 MUF.
MU-A-2018-86103-002: Random amplitudes/frequencies/phases generate a one-dimensional wave state.
MU-A-2018-86103-003: The PM spectrum supplies component energy for a fully developed sea.
MU-A-2018-86103-004: A double sum over frequency and direction yields a 3-D random wave surface.
MU-A-2018-86103-005: Free-space, ionosphere, reflection, and additional terms form the total ledger.
MU-A-2018-86103-006: The km/MHz FSPL formula and Earth-radius geometry provide path cost and hop range.
MU-A-2018-86103-007: A sunspot/zenith/frequency relation is printed, then numerical work fixes La at 4 dB.
MU-A-2018-86103-008: Complex seawater permittivity feeds horizontal/vertical coefficients and their equal-energy combination.
MU-A-2018-86103-009: A local tangent and reflected-path equation classify forward-reflecting micro-elements.
MU-A-2018-86103-010: An area/length shadow factor is composed with a forward fraction; Appendix also uses an empirical wind-height correction.
MU-A-2018-86103-011: The source logarithm minus path, absorption, reflection, and additional loss produces P1.

models.section: Signal field, atmospheric noise, and SNR
models.summary: MU-A-2018-86103-012: Transmitter/frequency/gain/loss determine Et; a lookup noise coefficient and bandwidth determine En.
MU-A-2018-86103-013: Distance grows as nDmax, ionosphere loss as nLa, and intermediate surface loss as (n-1)Lg.
MU-A-2018-86103-014: Ground permittivity/conductivity and relief level replace sea inputs to produce first-reflection and hop claims.
MU-A-2018-86103-015: The repeated SNR inequality binds hop losses to a 10 dB gate; r/v is called the same-path duration.
MU-A-2018-86103-016: Controlled slices connect intermediate coefficients to first-reflection power and threshold distance.
MU-A-2018-86103-017: A five-row table provides tropical/night/day/season frequency guidance without a quantitative optimizer.

verification.summary: 137.2+96.8-32.44 equals 201.56, confirming the algebraic combination behind Equation 22.
nLa and (n-1)Lg correctly count ionosphere passages and intermediate surface reflections under the stated topology.

n=1,2,3 distances round to 3225, 6449, and 9674 km.

r in km divided by ship speed in km/h yields hours.

weaknesses.summary: All 28 physical pages carry a red commercial watermark; the three front-matter pages precede a 25-page internally numbered body.
Equation 5 uses Li while the prose and Figure 4 use La for ionospheric absorption.
Equation 10 omits the minus sign used by the Appendix; coefficients below one therefore produce a negative quantity called loss.
Equation 19 and Notation use P0 as transmitter and P1 as first reflection, but the following prose reverses them.
Table 1 prints 100 MHz although the paper defines HF as 3-30 MHz and Figure 10 uses 10/20/30 MHz.
Table 4 says f=15 Hz; the model and code use 15 MHz.
Equation 20 says P is kW, while Table 4 and code insert 100 W as P=100, inflating SNR by at least 30 dB.
Equation 21 labels B in dB while code uses 0.003 without a declared Hz/kHz/MHz base; SNR can shift by tens of dB.
Equation 20 prose calls Gt 'tt(dB)', leaving the antenna-gain interface inconsistent.
The moving SNR inequality reuses label 24, label 26 is absent, and the next formula is 27.
Appendix uses 0.81 and 7400 plus a directional factor, unlike Equation 3 constants 8.1e-3 and 0.74.
Wave code computes sqrt(2*swi*wavewn*theta) with negative direction angles instead of positive thetawn, creating complex amplitudes.
The code plots abs(z), hiding complex amplitudes and altering wave statistics.
wavewp is unused and the code lacks Equation 4's time term, so it generates only one random snapshot.
The paper states epsilon_ij in [0,pi/2], but code samples rand*2*pi.
Equation 15 prose calls the input theta while the equation uses Delta; xi'(x) is not explicitly evaluated at x0.
Equation 16 intends forward reflections, but the variable definition describes m as positive and negative reflected waves together.
Equation 17 is derived from a 2-D cross section but calls S and s surface areas without a 3-D mapping.
The prose describes the left panel as angles and the right as frequencies, opposite the plotted legends.
Figure 8 code uses 15/180*2, about 9.55 degrees, rather than 15/180*pi.
Fresnel code fixes sigma=50 S/m, outside Table 3's 1-4.3 S/m range and reference value 4.
Table 3 labels relative-like permittivity values 80 and 4 as F/m, inconsistent with the Fresnel interface.
Figure 9 maps wind levels 0/2/4/6 directly to heights 0/1.5/3/4.5 without connecting to h=0.0051v^2.
Figure 11 code constructs complex permittivity then overwrites it with epsilon=8, eliminating conductivity and Table 3 materials.
The ground section claims diffraction/obstacle blocking but provides no diffraction equation, geometry, loss term, or code.
Figure 11's right axis remains labelled sea-surface reflection loss although the plot is presented as ground.
Figure 13 code writes the vertical calculation into RHh again, leaving RHv at zero.
Figure 13's reflection combination omits Equation 10's division by two and inherits only one polarization branch.
The printed Figure 13 SNR assignment ends at -(n-1)* and cannot execute from the PDF.
The prose says fsolve yields n=6, but Appendix only hard-codes for n=1:6 and has no threshold stop.
Figures 10/12 and Tables 4-5 lack complete generating code and parameter-to-output bindings.
Front-matter Figure 2 repeats all Figure 12 ground data but relabels relief degree as wind scale and sea behavior.
Numerical work fixes La=4 dB despite Summary/Strengths claims of periodic ionosphere analysis and optimal frequency.
The 0.85 MUF rule has no electron-density/MUF calculation and is not connected to frequency sweeps or Table 5.
Table 4 gives n=5,6 only as <10125 km at exactly 10 dB, without actual maximum distances or a solver rule.
tmax=r/v divides total radio path distance by ship speed, not remaining ship movement within a fixed multi-hop coverage geometry.
No seed, repeats, confidence intervals, direction/grid convergence, or error bars support the random-wave and sensitivity outputs.
The calm-sea six-hop, ground four-hop, and turbulent Table 4 threshold claims are not distinguished by complete comparable parameter bundles.

independent_extensions.summary: Repair power/bandwidth units and publish one complete link-budget ledger.
Replace the fixed La proxy with time/location/solar-conditioned ionosphere data and a real MUF gate.
Unify the prose micro-element/shadow algorithm with the empirical Appendix roughness correction.
Repair wave generator direction weighting, phase convention, time state, seeds, and convergence tests.
Use consistent complex material parameters across sea, freshwater, soil, and terrain branches.
Implement diffraction/obstacle geometry before claiming a ground blocking model.
Replace hard-coded hop loops with a validated integer threshold search using true slant path.
Define moving-ship coverage geometry and compute remaining-path time rather than total radio range divided by ship speed.
Bind every figure/table to an executable script, environment, and parameter manifest.
Validate wave, reflection, and received-field outputs against independent simulations and observations.
